texts.preamble: Sh. Ramashray Singh vs Sohan Lal on 13 October, 2022 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 354/21 Ramashray Singh v. Sohan Lal Cnr No.: Dlse01-003707-2021 Sh. Ramashray Singh S/o Late Sukhadev Singh R/o Jayamagal, Anchal Sheikhapura, Bihar. Presently at: F-42, Harkesh Nagar, Okhla, Phase-I, New Delhi-110020. .....Petitioner Versus 1. Sohan Lal S/o Sh. Ramphal R/o K-13, Yamuna Apartment, Holi Chowk, Village-Devli, Delhi. ............Driver-cum-owner/Respondent no. 1 2. Go Digit General Insurance Ltd. Through its Manager, 19, Spring Board,67-68 Chandra Building, Nehru Place, New Delhi-110065. .......Insurance Company/Respondent no. 2 Date of accident : 20.12.2019 Date of filing of Dar : 06.04.2021 Date of Decision : 13.10.2022 Mact No. 354/21 Ramashrey v. Sohan Lal Page No. 1 of 20 Bk Award 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 20.12.2019 at about 9.30 AM, petitioner/injured was going to his home at Harkesh Nagar Okhla after completing his night duty at Defence Colony, New Delhi. When he was going towards bus stand after crossing the road near Moolchand Flyover, offending vehicle i.e. scooty bearing no. DL-3S-CV-3994 which was coming from Hazrat Nizamuddin side hit the petitioner with a great force and petitioner fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Sh. Ramashray Singh vs Sohan Lal on 13 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112003481/ 1 3. It is further stated that after the accident someone called at 100 number for PCR and after some time PCR van came and took injured to Trauma Center, AIIMS where his MLC was prepared. 4. Further the FIR bearing No. 385/2019 u/s 279/337 IPC PS Lajpat Nagar was registered in this case. 5. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 05.08.2021 noticing 39% permanent physical impairment in relation to his right upper limb and both ear. 6. In response to petition, as per record driver-cum-owner/ respondent No.1 initially appeared, but did not file his reply and respondent no. 2/insurance company appeared and filed its reply and legal offer. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.08.2021 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic MACT No. 354/21 Ramashrey v. Sohan Lal Page No. 2 of 20 BK accident on 20.12.2020 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL 3SCU 3994 being driven & owned by R1 and insured with R3? OPP. 2. Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 8. It is noted that date of accident is inadvertently mentioned as 20.12.2020 in the issue no.1 while the same is 20.12.2019. Further, offending vehicle is insured with R-2 instead of R-3 as inadvertently mentioned in issue no.2. Same is noted and corrected accordingly as none of the parties has any objection to the same. 9. Further, as per record, Petitioner Ramashray Singh examined himself only as PW-1. Such PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1, Mark-A and Ex. PW-1/3 to Ex. PW-1/12. He was cross- examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-2 as well as by learned counsel for R-1/driver-cum-owner. 10. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 11. Further, as per record, None of the respondent led any evidence. Further, learned counsel for petitioner filed written arguments in prescribed form. Further, learned counsel for R-1 also filed written arguments alongwith copy of his driving licence. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person MACT No. 354/21 Ramashrey v. Sohan Lal Page No. 5 of 20 BK is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 21. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. Sh. Ramashray Singh vs Sohan Lal on 13 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112003481/ 4 (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 21.1. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of MACT No. 354/21 Ramashrey v. Sohan Lal Page No. 6 of 20 BK amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 21.3. 21.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 21.7. Further, it is argued by insurance company that at best loss of MACT No. 354/21 Ramashrey v. Sohan Lal Page No. 9 of 20 BK income for period of four months be granted in the present case whereas it is argued by learned counsel for petitioner that there is loss of income of six months is claimed. 2. Further in such case of Raj Kumar(Supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down a three step approach to decide compensation for the injured persons who have suffered permanent disability and same are as under: The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 34. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
